parsed.note: The claim traces cleanly from secondary media reporting → PIB Backgrounder → IMF Fintech Note → NPCI product statistics, with consistent wording ('more than 18 billion transactions per month') at every step; the only variation is that the PIB Backgrounder specifies the June 2025 figure as 18.39 billion while the IMF note (based on March 2025 NPCI data) uses the rounded 'more than 18 billion' form.

chain.title: UPI surge: India leads the world in fast payments; 18 billion monthly transactions power growth - Times of India
chain.exact_wording: According to data from the Press Information Bureau (PIB), UPI now processes over 18 billion transactions every month, accounting for 85 per cent of India's total digital payments.

chain.title: PIB Backgrounder
chain.exact_wording: Today, UPI processes over 18 billion transactions every month in India. / In June 2025 alone, it handled over ₹24.03 lakh crore in payments. This was spread across 18.39 billion transactions.
chain.change: PIB cites both the IMF note and NPCI as references; it rounds to 'over 18 billion' for the headline and gives the precise June 2025 figure (18.39 billion) separately. PIB is a government communicator, not the originating data authority.

chain.title: Growing Retail Digital Payments: The Value of Interoperability (IMF Fintech Note)
chain.exact_wording: UPI now processes more than 18 billion transactions per month and dominates other electronic retail payments in India. [footnote: UPI volume as of March 2025; see NPCI statistics here.]
chain.change: The IMF note is the analytical intermediary; it derives the 'more than 18 billion' figure from NPCI product statistics as of March 2025 and cites NPCI explicitly in a footnote, but does not independently collect the data.

chain.title: Unified Payments Interface (UPI) Product Statistics | NPCI
chain.date: ongoing (March 2025 data cited by IMF; page currently shows through October 2026)
chain.exact_wording: | October-2026 | 758 | 25,466.70 | 31,52,929.46 | [monthly table; March 2025 row, per IMF footnote, is the basis for the '18 billion' figure]
